items.title: Bret Michaels Cancels All 2026 Tour Dates for ‘Rest and Recovery’ After Recent Surgeries
items.summary:
Bret Michaels has scrapped the rest of his 2026 tour dates on doctors' orders, days after attempting a return to the stage following surgery. The Poison frontman, a Type 1 diabetic, recently had a kidney stone removed and a ureteral stent placed, and played a comeback show Friday night in Sugar Hill, Georgia.

That show turned out to be the problem. Doctors and paramedics evaluated Michaels immediately afterward and concluded he had not healed enough to keep working, according to a statement his representatives posted to social media. "Bret will be taking the next several months off to heal and get back to 100%," the statement read.

His medical team framed the decision as a matter of timing and conditions as much as recovery. "He wanted to attempt this show, but we feel there is a much-needed period of rest and slow recovery ahead, especially considering the heat and humidity during the summer months and the effect it can have on his blood sugar levels," the doctors said in the statement, as Rolling Stone reported.

Michaels addressed fans himself in a separate post, acknowledging he may have rushed back. "In my nonstop spirit to go out do what I love which is to play music and to see all of you, all my family, friends and fans meet everybody it's what I truly love I may have just chosen to go sooner than I should have," he wrote. "We will come back better than ever."

The cancellations wipe out eight remaining shows. Six dates on his Live and Amplified Tour were booked for August and September, including a headlining slot Saturday at The Mountain Music Festival in Gatlinburg, Tennessee, with two more gigs scheduled for November. No rescheduled dates have been announced.

items.title: ‘The Gentlemen’ Officially Renewed for Season 3 as First Season 2 Trailer Drops: ‘I’m Looking Forward to Pushing the Boundaries Further,’ Guy Ritchie Says (EXCLUSIVE)
items.summary:
Netflix has renewed "The Gentlemen" for a third season, ordering eight more episodes of Guy Ritchie's crime caper starring Theo James and Kaya Scodelario. The streamer confirmed the pickup the same day it released the first full trailer for Season 2, which arrives Sept. 3.

Ritchie will direct again and co-write with Matthew Read. "The ambition of 'The Gentlemen' has accelerated, the world has expanded and the consequences carry weight," Ritchie said. "A third season felt inevitable, and I'm looking forward to pushing the boundaries of it further."

Season 3 is in pre-production and due to start shooting imminently, though Variety reported that no scripts have been finalized and no new casting has been set, despite rumors that Meghan Markle would join. The renewal lands alongside a run of Netflix U.K. orders that includes Black Mirror Season 8, Legends Season 2, Being Gordon Ramsay Season 2, and second seasons of Supacell, Black Doves and House of Guinness.

The new season sends Eddie Horniman and Susie Glass abroad, expanding their operation to lakeside villas in Italy. Eddie's climb through the criminal world runs parallel to his ascent in the British establishment, where he meets an aristocrat played by Hugh Bonneville, new to the cast. "Four hundred years ago, this estate spread out as far as the eye could see. I want it all back," Eddie tells Geoff in the trailer, while Giancarlo Esposito's American billionaire Stanley Johnston tells him, "You are destined to rule, forge your own path."

Ray Winstone returns as kingpin Bobby Glass, with Harry Goodwins as Jack, Joely Richardson as Lady Sabrina, Daniel Ings as Freddy, Jasmine Blackborow as Charly and Vinnie Jones as Geoff. Esposito, Michael Vu, Ruby Sear and Pearce Quigley are also back, joined by Benjamin Clementine, Benedetta Porcaroli, Amra Mallassi, Tyler Conti, boxer Chris Eubank Jr. and Love Island U.K. host Maya Jama.

Moonage Pictures produces for Netflix and Miramax TV, with Ritchie, Read, Ivan Atkinson, Will Gould, Simon Crawford, Collins and Frith Tiplady executive producing for Moonage, and Jonathan Glickman and Marc Helwig for Miramax TV.

items.title: Foo Fighters Play First-Ever Hollywood Bowl Show With LA Philharmonic
items.summary:
Foo Fighters played the Hollywood Bowl for the first time on Saturday, Aug. 22, stepping away from their Take Cover Tour for a one-night collaboration with the Los Angeles Philharmonic. Conductor Gustavo Dudamel and the Youth Orchestra Los Angeles joined the band for a 15-song set, the first Bowl appearance in the group's more than three decades.

Backed by orchestra and choir, the band opened with "Times Like These" and worked through "All My Life," "The Pretender," "Walk," "My Hero," "Learn to Fly," "The Sky Is a Neighborhood" and "Run." Dave Grohl dedicated "Aurora" to late drummer Taylor Hawkins, and the set ended with "Best of You," "Home" and "Everlong."

The setlist leaned on material the band rarely touches live. As Billboard noted, "I Should Have Known," from 2011's Wasting Light, got its first performance since 2012; "Razor," from 2005's In Your Honor, returned for the first time since 2006; and "Home," from Echoes, Silence, Patience & Grace, had not been played since 2007. The band also revived "A320," a 1998 Godzilla soundtrack cut originally built around string arrangements.

The show was part of "Celebrating Gustavo at the Bowl," a four-night tribute to Dudamel's 17th and final season as the LA Philharmonic's music and artistic director. He takes over as music director of the New York Philharmonic starting with the 2026-27 season. Grohl had already performed with Dudamel and the orchestra at Coachella 2025, on orchestral versions of "The Sky Is a Neighborhood" and "Everlong."

The Bowl date fell in a crowded stretch for the band, which played Rock in Rio in Brazil and filled in for the Pretty Reckless on a support slot for AC/DC in St. Louis beforehand. The Take Cover Tour, a stadium run marking the group's fourth decade, picks back up in mid-September with North American dates.

items.title: Television’s Richard Lloyd Diagnosed with Bile Duct Cancer, GoFundMe Launched
items.summary:
Richard Lloyd, the co-founding guitarist of Television, has been diagnosed with cholangiocarcinoma, a form of bile duct cancer. His bandmate in the Richard Lloyd Group, Sean Seymour, has launched a GoFundMe to help cover his medical and living expenses.

The fundraiser describes tumors in Lloyd's liver, including one sitting close enough to a major blood vessel that surgeons cannot safely remove it. "He has been in the ICU seven times, dealing with serious complications including sepsis twice, as well as complications involving his liver and kidneys," the page reads. "And through all of this, he's fighting."

Consequence reported that the campaign is aiming for $80,000, with the money going toward Lloyd and his wife Sheila, who has become a full-time caregiver while he is unable to work. Patti Smith and Susan Tweedy, wife of Wilco's Jeff Tweedy, have already donated.

Lloyd addressed supporters directly in a statement on the page. "I am usually a pretty upbeat person and I am taking this in stride, but it has become very difficult on our own and financially we are strapped," he said. "That's why I'm asking for your help. If you can see your way clear to make a donation please do that. Otherwise, please pass it around to your friends that might help and people that know me."

items.title: Ricky Martin Revealed As Cast Member Of Gael García Bernal’s ‘Hombre Al Agua’ In First Trailer & Image – Venice/TIFF
items.summary:
Ricky Martin appears in Gael García Bernal's new film "Hombre al Agua" and served as an executive producer on it, a detail kept quiet until the release of the first trailer and image ahead of the movie's festival run. Deadline reported the news exclusively, noting Martin joined the project on the eve of its shoot in Mérida, in Mexico's Yucatán.

The comedy-drama is Bernal's third feature as director, and he also co-wrote and produced it. Bernal stars as Camilo, a Cuban lifeguard who pulls Abel, a Mexican businessman with political ambitions, out of the Caribbean. Abel hires him as a right-hand man in Mexico, Camilo marries the businessman's daughter, and the new life gradually reveals itself as something other than what it appeared.

Martin plays Roby, an actor hired to portray Camilo in a biographical film that Camilo's wife is pushing forward. The cast also includes Esmeralda Pimentel, Débora Nascimento, Natalia Oreiro, Anna Díaz, Manuel García Rulfo and Jorge Salinas.

Bernal said he had wanted Martin from the start but assumed it was out of reach. "The part only required one day of shooting, so we kept saying, 'We'll find someone.' Then, shortly before we started shooting, I managed to get his number and called him. Before I had even really explained the project, he said, 'Whatever you want,'" the director said. The role is Martin's first fully Spanish-language screen part in more than two decades; he was most recently seen as bartender Robert Diaz on Apple TV+'s "Palm Royale."

Bernal produces with Diego Luna through their company La Corriente del Golfo, alongside Fernanda de la Peza and Stacy Perskie. Co-written with Mariano Pensotti, the film grew out of Bernal's own experience of fatherhood and the isolation he began to notice in it, and takes in masculinity, class, immigration and friendship.

"Hombre al Agua" world premieres in Venice's Spotlight section, then plays Toronto as a special presentation, with a Mexican theatrical release set for Sept. 24. It is one of 17 titles under consideration to represent Mexico at the 99th Academy Awards, a list that also includes Luna's "Ashes" and Fernando Eimbcke's "Flies."
